nodes.label: OpenCode Support Design Plan
nodes.author: Bot & Jesse
nodes.rationale: Extracting common skill discovery/parsing logic into lib/skills-core.js allows code reuse between Codex and OpenCode implementations. OpenCode has JavaScript/TypeScript plugins with event hooks and custom tools API, unlike Claude Code (native plugin) and Codex (bootstrap + CLI).

nodes.label: Skills Improvements from User Feedback
nodes.rationale: Two Claude instances provided detailed feedback from real development scenarios revealing systematic gaps in current skills: verification gaps (verifying operations succeed but not that they achieve intended outcomes), process hygiene (background processes accumulate and interfere across subagents), context optimization (subagents get too much irrelevant information), self-reflection missing (no prompt to critique own work before handoff), and mock safety (mocks can drift from interfaces without detection).

nodes.label: Drill (eval harness)
nodes.rationale: Drill is a Python skill-compliance benchmark harness that drives real tmux sessions, runs LLM actors and verifiers, supports multiple CLI tools (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI), and is being migrated into governed-superpowers under evals/

nodes.label: evals/ directory
nodes.rationale: The new canonical eval harness location in governed-superpowers containing full drill source, scenarios, fixtures, prompts, backend configs, and tests

nodes.label: Subagent-gated verification protocol
nodes.rationale: Every change in the implementation plan gets cross-checked by an independent subagent before commit. Bash test deletions require per-assertion mapping to drill scenarios; drill SHA verification, checksum matching, path defaults changes all require subagent verification gates

nodes.label: Task-scoped review dispatch
nodes.rationale: Per-task reviews scoped to the task: diff-first reading, justified broadening, no redundant test runs. Final whole-branch review keeps breadth. Design makes reviews cheaper without weakening them by stopping redundant work and scoping prompts

nodes.label: Cost iteration results
nodes.rationale: Live eval runs showed per-task spec and quality reviews merged into one task-reviewer-prompt.md (one reviewer, two verdicts), turn-count-beats-token-price model guidance, Important severity calibrated to merge-blocking maintainability damage, diff handed to reviewers as a file. Final frozen config: go-fractals 44.4 min / 13.4M / $11.67 (-32% time, -37% tokens, -27% dollars vs baseline)

nodes.label: Positive-instruction design doctrine
nodes.rationale: Micro-tests on opus (5 reps per phrasing, programmatic scoring) measured that composition prohibitions backfire when the model has its own agenda for the output (restating specs feels like helpful curation), but tripwires work, recognition tables work, discrete-directive prohibitions work when the model has no competing incentive. Doctrine: lead with positive recipes, drop prohibition halves when they are dead weight, ties go to shorter phrasing

nodes.label: Strict-cost SDD experiment ladder
nodes.rationale: Minimize dollars per plan-execution with hard invariants on quality (sdd-quality-reviewer-catches-planted-defect pass rate N=5, blind A/B deliverable parity) and judgment (cheapen mechanics never judgment). Ladder: L1 plan-side crispness (task right-sizing, structured constraints header, per-task Interfaces line, per-task model-tier recommendation), L2 controller tier (expensive model at plan time, mid-tier execution with explicit escalation rules), L3 reviewer tier (haiku-with-package, likely to die on judgment guardrail), L4 resident-context diet

nodes.label: L1 Plan-side crispness
nodes.rationale: Status 2026-06-11: elicitation tested end-to-end; cost win belongs to opus-written complete-code plans (hand-written prose fixture plans are ~2× costlier to execute); the guidance owns fidelity and variance instead: deterministic constraints propagation, exact cross-task interfaces, fix waves 1 vs 2-4. The writing-plans PR claims those grounds, not dollars

nodes.label: L2 Controller tier
nodes.rationale: Status 2026-06-11: DIED AT THE GATES. Recon was positive ($6.68/$8.05, mechanics clean). Escalation scenarios (explicit plan self-contradiction) passed 5/5 at sonnet. But planted-defect battery failed decisively: sonnet controller's per-task quality gate collapsed into plan-compliance advocacy, defect shipped 4/5 runs, only tier-pinned opus final reviewer caught it. Cheap controllers handle explicit escalation but absorb implicit authority-vs-quality adjudication

nodes.label: L3 Reviewer tier
nodes.rationale: Status 2026-06-11: DEAD. Planted-defect ×5 with forced-haiku task reviewers: 2 pass / 1 indeterminate / 2 fail (baseline 5/5); haiku cleanly flagged 0 of 10 planted defects at correct severity — 1 found-but-downgraded with exact prohibited rationale, 9 missed or rationalized. Cheap reviewers fail by advocating for defects; passing runs survived only on controller redundancy or final review

nodes.label: Visual companion auth hardening
nodes.rationale: Fix security and reliability gaps in PR #1720 brainstorming visual companion without changing core workflow or adding runtime dependencies. Design: bootstrap keyed loads (GET /?key=token returns bootstrap that stores key in sessionStorage and navigates to bare /), WebSocket same-origin enforcement (origin must match request target origin), helper reconnect credential (reads key from sessionStorage for ws:// URL), /files/* containment (realpath containment boundary), leak-reduction headers, gitignore durable session state

nodes.label: Visual companion final hardening fixup
nodes.rationale: Finish PR #1720 hardening pass with clean security behavior, deterministic tests, and PR diff containing only companion work. Design: rebase onto current dev (resolve evals submodule conflict), root screen containment (same guard as /files/*), fallback token isolation (port fallback must not reuse persisted .last-token), stop-server ownership proof (per-start server instance id as inert command-line argument, signal only when target process argv contains exact --brainstorm-server-id=id), test hardening (deterministic across macOS and Windows Git Bash)

nodes.label: SDD plan-scoped workspace
nodes.rationale: SDD's durable-progress workspace (.governed-superpowers/sdd/) has no plan identity and no end-of-life. Every artifact keyed by bare task number causes cross-plan collisions, git contamination, and stale state accumulation. Design: per-plan workspace directory .governed-superpowers/sdd/<plan-slug>/, ledger names its plan (first line: # SDD ledger — plan: docs/governed-superpowers/plans/<plan-file>.md), workspace end-of-life (controller deletes plan's workspace after final review clean and fix wave merged)

nodes.label: Plan-scoped workspace eval RED outcome
nodes.rationale: RED outcome that forced re-scope (maintainer decision, Jesse, 2026-07-06): the originally hypothesized failure — a controller blindly adopting a stale foreign ledger as its own progress — did NOT reproduce: 25/25 reps across three framings forensically cross-checked the ledger's cited commits against git history and plan files, refused the foreign ledger, and started plan B at Task 1 — spending 6–13 tool calls of cross-plan forensics per resume to do so

nodes.label: Plan-scoped workspace eval GREEN results
nodes.rationale: S1 GREEN 5/5 resolved structurally (workspace + identity line), none via commit-content forensics; tool_uses 9/11/9/7/12 vs RED probe mean 9.0. S2 GREEN (regression) 5/5 recognized Tasks 1-2 as complete, dispatched Task 3; tool_uses 11/9/7/8/7 vs S2 RED control mean 7.8. Structural claim: no GREEN rep needed content forensics to disambiguate, and misattribution is now impossible when every ledger names its plan

nodes.label: SDD fix-loop redesign
nodes.rationale: Make the subagent-driven-development skill's review-fix loop convergent and autonomous, and make the document readable, without rewriting eval-tuned language. Design decisions: original implementer fixes its own review findings (resume it in place), re-reviews scoped to the findings, circuit breaker at five fix rounds (three resumes, then two fresh dispatches on more capable model), at trip the controller adjudicates and routes, reorganize SKILL.md by lifecycle preserving tuned sentences, convert Red Flags to rationalization table

nodes.label: Fix loop mechanism
nodes.rationale: Rounds 1–3 resume the original implementer with findings verbatim; rounds 4–5 fresh implementer on more capable model with full task context; every round's re-review is scoped (brief, updated report, original findings list, fix-scoped diff package); fix-report completeness gate before re-review; no early exit (controller never adjudicates before the cap); Minor findings never enter the loop. At trip after round five fails, controller judges each open finding: contested/wrong (ledger with adjudication), real not load-bearing (ledger as known-open), real and load-bearing (BLOCKED stop)

nodes.label: Plugin tests (tests/ directory)
nodes.rationale: Bash + node + python integration tests for brainstorm-server JS, OpenCode plugin loading, codex-plugin sync, and analysis utilities. Does the plugin's non-LLM code work?

nodes.label: Skill behavior evals (evals/ directory)
nodes.rationale: Python harness driving real tmux sessions of Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI, with LLM actor and verifier judging skill compliance. Drill scenarios at evals/scenarios/*.yaml. Slow (3-30+ minutes each), run real LLM sessions, not part of CI today

nodes.label: run-hook.cmd (polyglot dispatcher)
nodes.rationale: Cross-platform polyglot dispatcher for hook scripts. Windows treats first block as batch commands, Unix shells treat it as no-op heredoc. Validates script name, resolves hook directory, tries bash in three places on Windows, execs named extensionless script on Unix. Scripts are extensionless to prevent Claude Code's Windows .sh-auto-prepend from interfering

nodes.label: brainstorming skill
nodes.rationale: Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue. HARD-GATE: Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. Checklist: explore project context, offer visual companion just-in-time, ask clarifying questions one at a time, propose 2-3 approaches, present design in sections, write design doc, spec self-review, user reviews written spec, transition to implementation by invoking writing-plans skill

nodes.label: Visual companion
nodes.rationale: Browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool, not a mode. Decide per-question whether to use browser (UI mockups, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual comparisons, design polish, spatial relationships) or terminal (requirements/scope questions, conceptual A/B/C choices, tradeoff lists, technical decisions, clarifying questions). Server watches directory for HTML files and serves newest one to browser. Content fragments vs full documents: write content fragments by default (server wraps in frame template), only write full documents when complete control needed

nodes.label: Frame template HTML
nodes.rationale: Provides consistent frame with OS-aware light/dark theming, header branding and connection status, scrollable main content area, CSS helpers for common UI patterns (options for A/B/C choices, cards for visual designs, mockup container, split view, pros/cons, placeholder, inline mockup elements, typography and sections)

nodes.label: Spec document reviewer prompt template
nodes.rationale: Use when dispatching a spec document reviewer subagent after spec document written to docs/governed-superpowers/specs/. Check completeness (TODOs, placeholders, TBD, incomplete sections), consistency (contradictions, conflicting requirements), clarity (ambiguous requirements), scope (focused enough for single plan), YAGNI (unrequested features, over-engineering). Output: Status (Approved | Issues Found), Issues (if any), Recommendations (advisory, do not block approval)

nodes.label: dispatching-parallel-agents skill
nodes.rationale: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies. Core principle: dispatch one agent per independent problem domain, let them work concurrently. Pattern: identify independent domains, create focused agent tasks (specific scope, clear goal, constraints, expected output), dispatch in parallel (multiple dispatch calls in one response), review and integrate. When NOT to use: related failures, need full context, exploratory debugging, shared state

nodes.label: executing-plans skill
nodes.rationale: Use when you have a written implementation plan to execute in a separate session with review checkpoints. Process: load and review plan (ensure isolated workspace, read plan file, review critically, raise concerns or create todos), execute tasks (mark in_progress, follow steps exactly, run verifications, mark completed), complete development (invoke finishing-a-development-branch skill after all tasks complete and verified). Note: tell partner Governed-Superpowers works much better with access to subagents; if available use subagent-driven-development instead

nodes.label: finishing-a-development-branch skill
nodes.rationale: Use when implementation complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work. Core principle: Verify tests → Detect environment → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up. Step 1: run full test suite (if fail report and stop). Step 2: detect environment (GIT_DIR vs GIT_COMMON to determine menu and cleanup). Step 3: determine base branch. Step 4: present options (normal repo and named-branch worktree: 3 options; detached HEAD: 2 options). Step 5: execute choice (merge locally, push and create PR, keep as-is, discard if explicit request). Step 6: cleanup workspace (provenance-based for Governed-Superpowers-created worktrees)

nodes.label: receiving-code-review skill
nodes.rationale: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable. Core principle: verify before implementing, ask before assuming, technical correctness over social comfort. Response pattern: READ complete feedback, UNDERSTAND restate requirement or ask, VERIFY check against codebase reality, EVALUATE technically sound for THIS codebase, RESPOND technical acknowledgment or reasoned pushback, IMPLEMENT one at a time test each. Forbidden responses: performative agreement ('You're absolutely right!', 'Great point!', 'Let me implement that now' before verification)

nodes.label: requesting-code-review skill
nodes.rationale: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements. Core principle: review early, review often. Dispatch code reviewer subagent to catch issues before they cascade. Mandatory: after each task in subagent-driven development, after completing major feature, before merge to main. How to request: get git SHAs, dispatch general-purpose subagent filling code-reviewer.md template with DESCRIPTION, PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS, BASE_SHA, HEAD_SHA, act on feedback

nodes.label: Code reviewer prompt template
nodes.rationale: Template for dispatching code reviewer subagent. Review completed work against requirements and code quality standards before it cascades. What to check: plan alignment, code quality, architecture, testing, production readiness. Calibration: categorize issues by actual severity, acknowledge what was done well, flag deviations from plan, flag issues with plan itself. Output format: Strengths, Issues (Critical Must Fix / Important Should Fix / Minor Nice to Have), Recommendations, Assessment (Ready to merge Yes | No | With fixes, Reasoning)
